guide.title: Concepts Guide
guide.bottomUp: From bottom to top: Feature → Scenario → Flow → Set → Cycle → Plan
guide.description: Pehape organizes tests in a five-level hierarchy. Understanding when to use each concept allows you to design clear, reusable and easy to maintain test campaigns.
guide.containersDescription: Each level can contain one or more elements of the lower level. Feature and Scenario are the source of the tests; the upper levels are ways to organize them.

feature.title: Feature
feature.subtitle: Gherkin's .feature file
feature.description: A .feature file is the test writing unit. It contains several scenarios (Scenarios) grouped and related to a single system functionality, written in natural language (Gherkin).
whenToUse: Document a complete system functionality
Group related scenarios under a single context
Describe the expected behavior from the user's perspective

scenario.title: Scenario
scenario.subtitle: The individual test case
scenario.description: A Scenario is the minimum executable unit. It defines a specific system behavior through a sequence of Given / When / Then steps. It is associated with tags to filter and categorize execution.
whenToUse: Test a specific use case or flow
Verify a specific system behavior
Reuse as a building block in a Test Flow
scenario.mnemonic: What specific behavior am I testing?
scenario.example: Scenario: Successful withdrawal with sufficient balance

test-flow.title: Test Flow
test-flow.subtitle: The ordered sequence of scenarios
test-flow.description: A Test Flow is a sequence of Scenarios (from one or more Features) organized in the canvas to be executed in a specific order. It is the "flow" that you design by dragging scenarios from the library. A Test Flow can only contain Scenarios. ⚠️ Execution rule — Fail-Fast: if a Scenario within a Flow fails, all remaining Scenarios in that same Flow are skipped automatically. Execution continues with the next Flow or Cycle; the global Plan is never stopped due to a Flow failure.
whenToUse: Define the execution order of a set of scenarios
Compose complex flows: login → navigate → action → logout
Ensure dependencies between test steps
Isolate a block of scenarios with its own Fail-Fast behavior (failure in one does not affect other Flows)
test-flow.mnemonic: In what order do I execute these scenarios?
test-flow.example: Main Flow: login → withdrawal → check balance → logout

test-set.title: Test Set
test-set.subtitle: The matrix generator of flows
test-set.description: A Test Set groups Features and/or Test Flows logically (no longer loose scenarios). It acts as a multiplier: if you add a Feature (which has multiple scenarios) along with other flows, it will internally create an execution matrix. For example, when joining [Flow A] + [Feature B with 2 scenarios] + [Flow C], the Set will generate two resulting flows: (Flow A + Scenario B1 + Flow C) and (Flow A + Scenario B2 + Flow C). ⚠️ Design entity only — the Test Set does not exist at runtime. Before the orchestrator starts, each Set is expanded using Cartesian Product and becomes N independent Test Flows. Each resulting Flow inherits the normal Fail-Fast behavior: a failure in one combination does not affect other combinations of the same Set.
whenToUse: Group multiple Test Flows and Features under a single purpose
Create matrix combinations of scenarios with common pre/post condition steps
Organize large modules of an application in the same grouping
When you need the same pre/post-condition to combine with multiple scenario variants
test-set.mnemonic: How do I logically group these flows and features?
test-set.example: Payment Test Set, User Validation Set

test-cycle.title: Test Cycle
test-cycle.subtitle: The iteration or test round
test-cycle.description: A Test Cycle groups one or more Test Sets and/or Test Flows under a specific test iteration. It represents a complete "round": it can contain multiple parallel sets or flows that run together.
whenToUse: Group sets and flows under the same round or sprint of tests
Organize regression tests, smoke tests, or sanity checks
Separate executions by environment (staging, production)
test-cycle.mnemonic: In which iteration/round do I execute these sets and flows?
test-cycle.example: Weekly Regression Cycle, Sprint 12 - Smoke Tests

test-plan.title: Test Plan
test-plan.subtitle: The root campaign container
test-plan.description: The Test Plan is the highest level container. It groups all the cycles of a complete test campaign. It has its own state (draft → running → completed) and can be scheduled for automatic execution.
whenToUse: Organize a complete test campaign (quarterly, by version)
Schedule automatic executions of the cycle set
Have a global view of the status of all tests
test-plan.mnemonic: To which campaign does all this belong?
test-plan.example: Q2 2026 Test Plan, Release v3.5 — Regression Suite
